title: Rigidity of Averages over the Two Largest Prime Factors
summary: Let \(P_1(n)\) and \(P_2(n)\) be the largest and second-largest distinct prime factors of \(n\), respectively. Alladi and Johnson asked whether there exists a bounded function \(f\) on the primes for which both limits \(\frac{1}{x}\sum_{2\le n\le x} f(P_1(n)) \longrightarrow κ_1\) and \(\frac{1}{x}\sum_{2\le n\le x} f(P_2(n)) \longrightarrow κ_2\) exist with \(κ_1\neqκ_2\), where we set \(f(P_2(n))=0\) when \(n\) is a prime power. We prove that this is impossible: convergence of the first average forces convergence of the second to the same limit. On the \(\log\log\)-scale, the two averages…
